canonical.name: Cotangent phase-space definition and action dimensions
canonical.support: A page-local definition fixes the omega sign, the intrinsic observable domain and model dimensional conventions.

canonical.name: Temporal chart with lapse, shift and positive slice metric
canonical.support: A local chart definition distinguishes the normal observer from the coordinate time vector and states every chart hypothesis.

canonical.name: Almost-regular Legendre hypotheses
canonical.support: Constant rank, embedded image, surjective-submersion and connected-fibre conditions are stated as assumptions.

canonical.name: Background and model quantities
canonical.support: The physics definition separates primitive model parameters, quantity definitions and empirical claims.

canonical.name: Regular primary constraint system
canonical.support: The constraint surface, weak equality and multiplier units are fixed locally.

canonical.name: Regular first-class local leaf space
canonical.support: A full local proof adds smooth parameter-dependent ODE and Frobenius steps; no global quotient is asserted.

canonical.name: Positive homogeneity and Legendre degeneracy
canonical.support: The Euler identity and Hessian-kernel argument are given in full.

canonical.name: Flat shifted chart and negative coordinate Hamiltonian
canonical.support: An explicit invertible coordinate change verifies flatness and the exact sign and speed inequalities.

sources.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes (arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1)
sources.locator: Complete 238-page notes; Chapter 1, printed pp. 25–27, and Chapter 3, printed pp. 68–72; full relevant sections inspected.

contents.name: Chapter 1: worldlines, proper time and energy-momentum vector
contents.support: The length and momentum conventions are used as definitions; no empirical clock or particle claim is inferred.

contents.name: Chapter 3: geodesics and affine parameters
contents.support: The local first-order proof derives the reparameterized geodesic equation and makes no global completeness claim.

contents.name: Chapter 3: first variation of the proper-time functional
contents.support: The local argument independently differentiates the curve functional, integrates the endpoint term and obtains the affine equation.

sources.title: Andrew Hanson, Tullio Regge and Claudio Teitelboim, Constrained Hamiltonian Systems, Part 1
sources.locator: Complete 35-page Part 1 PDF; Chapter I, printed pp. 7–11, and Chapter II, printed pp. 27–30; inspected in full over the named ranges.

contents.name: Chapter I, Formal Introduction: singular Lagrangians and constraints
contents.support: The definition keeps regularity explicit and does not infer a regular surface from singularity alone.

contents.name: Chapter I, Formal Introduction: constraint consistency and first/second class
contents.support: The scaffold derives the tangency equation and explicitly makes no universal termination claim.

contents.name: Chapter II, Relativistic Point Particle
contents.support: The flat example proves its own complete quotient and global slice instead of presuming a global quotient.

contents.name: Chapter II, second-class constraints and Dirac bracket
contents.support: The local proof establishes tangent fields, restricted nondegeneracy, extension independence and the induced Jacobi identity.

sources.title: Ghanashyam Date, Lectures on Constrained Systems, arXiv:1010.2062
sources.locator: Complete 28-page PDF; §3 “Constrained Lagrangian and Hamiltonian Systems” and §4 “Dirac’s Algorithm for Discovering Constraints”, printed pp. 12–22; inspected in full.

contents.name: §3 Constrained Lagrangian and Hamiltonian Systems: multiplier consistency
contents.support: The local theorem proves the tangency equation and lists its possible algebraic outcomes.

contents.name: §3 claim of dimension-count finite termination for the full algorithm
contents.support: The assigned theorem stops at the consistency equation and does not claim that arbitrary new constraints or their ranks stabilize.
contents.reason: The section makes a broader finite-termination claim than this pair needs. The assigned result proves only the stated consistency equation and explicitly leaves further constraints to separate regularity checks.

contents.name: §4 Dirac’s Algorithm for Discovering Constraints: second-class bracket
contents.support: The complete local Dirac bracket proof supplies the restricted symplectic geometry and Poisson properties.

sources.title: W. F. Chagas-Filho, Free massless particles and extended space-time algebra, arXiv:hep-th/0401091v2
sources.locator: Complete 6-page paper; §§1–2, pp. 1–3, including the einbein action and massless constraint; full text inspected.

contents.name: §1 Introduction: einbein form and one-dimensional reparametrization covariance
contents.support: This source supports a separate positive-multiplier formulation; local content specifies SI units and the nonzero future-null branch.

contents.name: §2 Massless particles
contents.support: The null action is adopted separately and is not obtained by setting m=0 in the massive momentum identity.

contents.name: Extended space-time/conformal algebra beyond the free massless constraint
contents.support: The paper’s extended symmetry algebra is additional theory beyond the assigned cotangent phase, shell, reduction and action-dimension scope.
contents.reason: The extended conformal algebra is independent of the assigned shell and time-gauge results. The pair does not add a symmetry or quantization development, and its claims are not needed by the local proofs.

sources.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, complete lecture notes (arXiv:gr-qc/0703035)
sources.locator: Complete 220-page notes; §§3.3.1–3.3.3, printed pp. 41–44, and §§4.2.2–4.2.3, pp. 56–58; full relevant sections inspected.

contents.name: §3.3.1 Lapse function
contents.support: The chart definition states positive lapse, unit future normal and its distinct role from the coordinate time vector.

contents.name: §§3.3.2–3.3.3 Normal evolution vector and Eulerian observers
contents.support: The normal and coordinate time vector remain distinct in the page definition and subsequent observer-energy calculation.

contents.name: §4.2.2 Shift vector
contents.support: The chart definition specifies the shift as tangent to the spacelike slices.

contents.name: §4.2.3 3+1 metric components and line element
contents.support: The local proof independently inverts the lapse-shift metric and derives the future shell root and chart Hamiltonian.
